title: Apple Watch production study
summary: Connecting enclosure reverse engineering, drawings and production planning.
overview: An academic study of a watch enclosure and a proposed high-volume manufacturing process. This was university work, independent of Apple.
constraints: The geometry had to be reconstructed from limited public information. Production planning considered machining, tooling, throughput and cost.
contribution: The study was completed as a two-person academic project. This case describes the team’s scope.
approach: The work combined CAD and manufacturing drawings with machine selection, a Python nesting algorithm and bottleneck analysis.
results: The existing technical portfolio documents a proposed production line and cost model. These are study outputs, not an operating factory.
limits: Dimensions, material assumptions, tolerances and production calculations need to be interpreted within the academic model and its source information.
